newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian court jails bank employees for embezzlement.
newsitem.headline: Algerian court jails bank employees for embezzlement.

text.p: An Algerian court has sentenced four employees of a state-owned bank to six years imprisonment for embezzlement, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Thursday.

The four, a director of a local branch of the unnamed bank in the southern town of Adrar, and three other staff, were also ordered to pay back 555,000 dinars ($9,910) of the stolen money on top of 20,000 dinars ($357) fines for each, said APS.

The sentences earlier this month followed a series of trials by Algerian courts of scores of employees in state-owned firms for fraud in the past 14 months after President Liamine Zeroual vowed to crack down on corruption.

Zeroual appointed former justice minister Hamdani Ben Khalil as chief of the anti-corruption body, the National Observatory of Supervision and Coordination against Corruption, last November to spearhead the fight against fraud.

Algerian officials blame corruption for nurturing a lack of trust between average Algerians and their leaders, compounding the problems in Zeroual's task of trying to pull Algeria out of five years of civil strife in which about 60,000 people have died.
